E2-08-serological-relationship-bar-chart

A horizontal bar chart showing the relative amount of precipitate formed when rabbit anti-human serum is mixed with serum from different animals. Bars from longest to shortest: human (100), chimpanzee (very long, slightly shorter than human), gorilla (very long), baboon (Old World monkey, medium-long), spider monkey (New World monkey, medium), dog (short), pig (short), chicken (almost none). Beside the chart, a small row of test tubes with decreasing cloudiness. The bar lengths show the pattern only, no exact numbers other than human = 100.
E2-12-animal-phylogenetic-evolutionary-tree

An evolutionary tree of animals drawn as a branching tree on a soft background. At the base: a single-celled protozoan (Amoeba). Branches rising in order: Hydra (coelenterate), tapeworm (flatworm), roundworm (nematode), earthworm (annelid), then a branch splitting to an insect (arthropod) and a snail (mollusc). A main trunk continues to vertebrates: a fish, then a frog (amphibian), then a lizard (reptile), which splits into two branches ending in a bird and a mammal (goat). Water shown at the lower part of the tree, land above.
E2-13-sickle-cell-molecular-mutation

Diagram of the sickle-cell mutation in three linked rows. Top row: two short DNA strands side by side as coloured base sequences, normal (…C T G A G G…) and sickle (…C T G T G G…), with the single changed base A to T highlighted in red. Middle row: the corresponding short chains of amino acid beads, with the sixth bead (blue) in the normal chain and "valine" (red) in the sickle chain. Bottom row: a normal round biconcave red blood cell beside a sickle-shaped red blood cell.
E2-01-fossil-formation-stages

Five-stage diagram of fossil formation in a row of vertical cross-sections through ground and water. Stage 1: a fish dies and sinks to the bottom of a lake. Stage 2: the body is covered by a layer of mud and sand; soft parts decaying. Stage 3: only the skeleton remains, under more layers of sediment. Stage 4: many layers of rock above the skeleton, which is now grey stone (mineralised). Stage 5: the land surface has been lifted and eroded, and a palaeontologist with a brush uncovers the fossil skeleton on a hillside.
E2-02-sedimentary-rock-fossil-strata

A vertical cliff cross-section showing six stacked sedimentary rock layers in different soft earth colours, with fossils drawn in each: bottom layer with simple worm-like and jellyfish-like imprints and trilobites; next layer with fish fossils; next with an amphibian; next with reptile and dinosaur bones and fern leaves; next with an early mammal and a bird skeleton; top layer with modern mammal bones and flowering plant leaves. A vertical arrow on the left side pointing up.
E2-03-archaeopteryx-fossil-reconstruction

Reconstruction drawing of the fossil animal Archaeopteryx, shown both as a slab of pale limestone with the fossil skeleton and feather impressions, and beside it as a living-animal reconstruction in soft colours: a crow-sized creature with feathered wings, three clawed fingers on each wing, small teeth in its jaws and a long bony tail with feathers along both sides.
E2-07-human-vestigial-organs

An outline of a human body (front view, neutral, gender-neutral figure in soft beige) with small highlighted circles and leader lines to five vestigial structures: the ear muscles around the ear, the plica semilunaris in the inner corner of the eye (with a small enlarged eye inset), wisdom teeth at the back of the jaw (small skull inset), the appendix at the lower right of the abdomen (small inset of caecum and appendix), and the coccyx at the base of the spine (small inset of the lower spine).
E2-09-vertebrate-embryo-development-grid

A grid of vertebrate embryos at three stages of development, in five columns: fish, salamander (amphibian), turtle (reptile), chicken (bird) and human (mammal). Top row (earliest stage): all five embryos look very similar, curled, with a large head, visible pharyngeal pouches (gill pouches) in the neck region and a tail. Middle row: differences beginning to appear (fins, limb buds, beak, etc.). Bottom row: recognisable young of each animal. Draw in soft pinks and beiges, simple and accurate, not exaggerated.
E2-05-homologous-pentadactyl-forelimbs-comparison

Comparison of pentadactyl forelimbs side by side: human arm, bat wing, bird wing, whale flipper, horse front leg and frog front leg. In every limb, colour-code the matching bones consistently: humerus in yellow, radius and ulna in orange, carpals in green, metacarpals in blue, phalanges in purple. Show outlines of the skin or wing around each skeleton faintly.
E2-11-plant-phylogenetic-evolutionary-tree

Plant evolution diagram shown as a branching tree rising from water at the bottom to dry land at the top. At the base, in water, a green filamentous alga (Spirogyra). Branching upward onto damp ground: a moss and a liverwort (Marchantia). Next branch: a fern with fronds and a rhizome. Next: a gymnosperm (pine tree with cones). Topmost branch: a flowering plant (a hibiscus shrub with a flower and fruits). Along the side, an arrow labelled with trends.
E2-14-chromosome-structural-mutations

Four small diagrams of chromosome structure mutations, each showing a normal chromosome (a vertical bar divided into coloured bands labelled A B C D E F with a centromere between B and C) and the mutated chromosome beside it. Deletion: A B C E F (band D missing). Duplication: A B C D D E F (band D repeated). Inversion: A B C E D F (D and E reversed). Translocation: A B C D plus bands G H from a second, differently coloured chromosome attached at the end, with the second chromosome shown shortened.
E2-10-biogeography-lungfish-world-map

World map in soft flat colours with simple animal icons: lungfish icons in tropical Africa (including Nigeria), South America and Australia, connected by faint dashed lines; kangaroo and koala icons in Australia; finch icons on the Galápagos Islands with an arrow from South America; a lemur icon on Madagascar. An inset in a corner shows the outline of the supercontinent Gondwana with Africa, South America, Australia, Antarctica and India joined together.
E2-04-horse-evolution-stages-foot

Evolution of the horse in five steps from bottom-left to top-right, each showing a side view of the whole animal at relative size and, beneath it, a simplified front-foot skeleton. 1: small fox-sized Hyracotherium (Eohippus) in a forest, foot with four toes. 2: Mesohippus, goat-sized, three toes. 3: Merychippus, pony-sized, three toes with a large middle toe. 4: Pliohippus, one main toe with side splints. 5: modern Equus, large, single hoofed toe with tiny splint bones, on open grassland.
E2-06-analogous-insect-bird-wings

A simple flat scientific illustration comparing two wings side by side on a clean white background. 

On the left, an insect wing drawn as a flat, transparent membrane with several thin branching veins and no bones. 

On the right, a bird wing seen from above, showing long flight feathers along the edge. Inside the bird wing, show a simple visible skeleton: one upper arm bone, two forearm bones, and a small, narrow fused bone cluster at the wingtip with only two tiny pointed digits. 

Large, simple shapes with wide clear spacing between the two wings. Minimalist textbook diagram style with clear black outlines and plain colors. No text, no symbols, and no extra callouts.
